Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i assembled the community survey export for the Northbank Neighborhood Office after the spring survey closed on May 18. the export is a spreadsheet drawn from 612 submitted forms, and it covers responses received from April 3 through May 18. i made the file on May 22 from the survey platform's standard download. the platform showed 612 submissions when i downloaded it. the sheet has one row for each submission and 18 columns, including submission date, neighborhood, preferred contact method, and answers to the 14 survey questions. it does not include names, street addresses, or email addresses, because those fields were not part of the export settings i used.

I work as the office's temporary survey coordinator, and I prepared the file for review rather than publication. On May 23, I asked Maya Chen, the office's data analyst, to check the column labels and confirm that the neighborhood values matched the boundary list she maintains. Maya checked the labels and values on May 24. She found that “Old Mill” appeared in 17 rows, while the boundary list calls that area “Mill District.” She did not change the export. She sent me a separate note identifying the 17 rows and said that the wording should be reviewed before the file is shared outside the office. Her note also pointed out that three entries had a blank neighborhood field. Those entries still had answers to other questions, and they remained in the spreadsheet.

The file contains both complete and partial submissions. The platform marked 548 submissions as complete and 64 as partial. I left the partial submissions in the export because the office's survey plan says to retain every submitted form for the initial review. The completion label is not a column in the downloaded sheet, so I added it as column S using the platform's status report. I matched the status report to the export by submission ID, then removed the submission ID column before saving the review copy. The two files are stored in the office's restricted survey folder, and the review copy is named spring_survey_review_0522.xlsx. The platform report and spreadsheet each show the same total of 612 submissions.

I also noticed that the platform's response summary and the spreadsheet do not present the preferred-contact answers in the same order. The summary lists phone, email, and paper mail; the spreadsheet lists email, phone, and paper mail. The counts are 241 for email, 198 for phone, 109 for paper mail, and 64 blank. I have not reordered the spreadsheet or changed any answers. I included the counts in my cover note so that a reader would not assume the different order indicates a difference in the responses. Maya's label check did not include a review of those counts, and she did not verify the platform's summary.

1. Items for review before the export is sent:
   1. Decide whether “Old Mill” should be changed to “Mill District,” or whether the original response wording should stay as submitted. Maya identified the mismatch but did not make a change.
   2. Decide whether the three blank neighborhood entries should remain blank in any version prepared for sharing. They have not been assigned a neighborhood by me or Maya.
   3. Confirm whether the office wants the 64 partial submissions included in the copy for the recipient. The survey plan calls for keeping them in the initial review, but it does not say whether they should be included in a later shared copy.
   4. If the spreadsheet is reordered for readability, keep the response values attached to their existing question labels. I have not rearranged the columns.

On May 25, office manager Luis Ortega asked me to prepare a copy for the Northbank Library's community liaison, Priya Shah. Luis said the library plans to use the survey findings when scheduling its summer meeting hours, and he requested a spreadsheet rather than a chart. He did not ask me to send it directly to Priya. I have not sent the review copy to Luis, Priya, or the library. I am asking Luis to confirm that Priya is the intended recipient and to tell me whether he wants the copy sent to her or returned to him first. I am also asking Maya to review the four items above, since her earlier check covered labels and neighborhood values only.

The cover note currently says that the export contains 612 submissions, including 548 marked complete and 64 marked partial, and that the contact-method counts include 64 blank responses. It also describes the spreadsheet as an unmodified platform export with a status column added for review. That description needs to be read carefully: I removed the submission ID column from the review copy after using it to match the status report, so the copy is not identical to the original download. The original download remains in the restricted folder alongside the status report. I have not changed any survey answers, and the “Old Mill” entries and blank neighborhood fields remain as they were in the downloaded responses.

If Luis confirms Priya as the recipient, and if the office decides that the shared copy should include only complete submissions, I can make a separate copy with the 548 complete submissions and leave the review copy unchanged. If either condition is not met, I will not make that version on the basis of this request. The four review items still need answers before I prepare a version for sharing, particularly the neighborhood wording and whether the partial submissions belong in that version.
